About the data

About the data

Disposal wells: oil and gas wells bring up salty water along with the oil and gas, and much of it is injected back underground through disposal wells. Operators report each well's monthly injection to the Railroad Commission of Texas on Form H-10. The map shows the 885 disposal wells in the Texas part of the Delaware Basin that reported injection in 2024. Together they injected 3.2 billion barrels, 42% of all disposal reported in Texas that year. 2024 is used because later reports were still coming in when the data were downloaded.

What the volumes are: water injected at each disposal well. That shows where produced water ends up today. It is not a measure of the water produced at each lease.

The hubs: the answer to one question. If the water injected at these wells went to a fixed number of shared recycling hubs instead, where would the hubs sit so that the total of barrels times straight-line miles to the nearest hub is as small as possible? This is a p-median problem, solved for 3 to 10 hubs with the spopt package for R. The candidate sites are the centers of a grid of hexagons 5 miles across inside the Texas part of the basin, 353 sites in all. With 3 hubs the average barrel is 11.6 miles from its hub; with 10 it is 6.1 miles.

What it leaves out: roads, pipelines, land ownership, hub capacity, cost, water quality and the New Mexico side of the basin. Distance is a straight line. The hubs illustrate a method on public records. They are not siting recommendations.

Sources: injection volumes from the Railroad Commission of Texas Underground Injection Control database, October 31, 2026 release. Well locations are Railroad Commission surface locations compiled by Clearfork Intelligence. The basin outline is the U.S. Energy Information Administration's Delaware Basin boundary, cut at the Texas state line.

Produced water disposal on the Texas side of the Delaware Basin

Each dot is a disposal well in the Texas part of the Delaware Basin, sized by the water it injected in 2024: 3.2 billion barrels at 885 wells. The numbered circles are where shared recycling hubs would sit to be closest to that water. Move the slider to change the number of hubs.
